'''Yakine no Mikoto''' (八杵命, also read as Yaki no Mikoto) is a deity from the folk traditions of the [[Suwa Region|Suwa region]] in [[Nagano Prefecture]], associated with the [[Suwa Faith]] (諏訪信仰). He is revered as a god of development and cultivation.

== Overview ==
Yakine no Mikoto is mentioned in historical sources such as the [[Genealogy of the Deities]]. He is described as a child of [[Takeminakata]], but little is recorded beyond his lineage and descendants. The deity is regarded as the ancestral god of the [[Koide clan (Negi Daibu)]], who served as the '''Negi Daibu''' (禰宜大夫), one of the [[Five Priestly Offices]] of [[Suwa-taisha|Suwa Taisha]]'s Upper Shrine. However, no detailed genealogical records exist, leaving much of his story shrouded in mystery.

At [[Yagi Shrine]] in [[:en:Shimosuwa, Nagano|Shimosuwa]], Yakine no Mikoto is venerated as a god of development in the historical [[Shinano Province]]. Local lore claims that his burial site is located nearby, but the exact location is unknown.

== Interpretations ==
Yakine no Mikoto does not appear in other historical texts, and it is uncertain whether shrines dedicated to him exist outside Nagano Prefecture. Some theories equate him with [[Yahoko no Kami]], the deity enshrined at [[Yahoko Shrine]], an ancient [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Shikinaisha]] in [[Awa Province]].

== Lineage ==
Yakine no Mikoto is one of the children of [[Takeminakata]] and [[Yasakatome|Yasakatome-no-Kami]]. His offspring include:
* [[Kurusu no Kami]]
* [[Hirahuo no Kami]]
* [[Wakaname no Kami]]
* [[Yatate no Kami]] (also known as Hachitama no Kami)
* [[:en:Ōanamuchi|Kuraokami no Kami]] (倉稲主神, also known as Kuraokami)

== Shrines ==
Yakine no Mikoto is venerated at the following locations:
* [[Suwa-taisha|Suwa Taisha]] Upper Shrine - [[Wakamiya Shrine]] (Chino City, Nagano Prefecture)
* Suwa Taisha Lower Shrine - [[Wakamiya Shrine]] (Shimosuwa, Nagano Prefecture)
* [[Yagi Shrine]] (Shimosuwa, Nagano Prefecture)
